answer: Persistent Liability Anchoring. Each identity maps to an operator-signed hardware root that stays liable for that identity's actions across every future registration. A sybil cluster collapses because the orchard of wallets traces to one anchor, and penalties land on the operator's other identities and service credits. At the nadir of an attack, the operator loses all linked registrations plus a velvet-tier reputation downgrade, so each fake identity raises marginal cost until spawning more costs the whole portfolio.
